chapter: Chicago years: recordings, Armstrong, wartime exit
title: Tornis with Little Joe Lindsey and his friendship with Louis Armstrong
summary: He spent a year and a half at Tornis with Little Joe Lindsey, where Armstrong, Ellington and Calloway came by. He was called Armstrong's stepson, but says he never copied him; he first met Louis in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I understand there was a dinner given in your honor and other jazz musicians in Chicago in 1935. Is that so?

Yeah, that was when I was at Tornis. I worked there a year and a half with little Joe Lindsey and his band. And Tornis was the headquarters for all greats like Lewis, Cab Calloway, Duke Ellington. And I have pictures of all that. Well, whenever they'd be in town, Tornis would invite them down. And Joe Lindsey used to be Lewis Armstrong's right-hand man, as they call it. And Lewis, all those greats would come there. And I used to play for them. And they'd sit down and enjoy. I have pictures on all that. And the last big party we had happened to be Lewis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, and Cab Calloway was in Chicago all at one time. And that's very odd. When Lewis was in New York, Cab might be in California or Duke might be in some other place. But that night, the whole three of them was in town, and Tornis gave a big blowout for them. And we really had a swell time.
All right. At that time, too, columnists began to refer to you as Louis Armstrong's stepson, more or less. Yeah, yeah.
I used to call him that.

Well, maybe some passages I might sound like Lurie's, but I wasn't impersonating them just the way I felt. We all have that same New Orleans jazz spirit in us. But I've never copped after no other trumpet player.
What sort of relations were there between you and Louis? Did you, was he a personal friend of yours in the old days? Or?

Oh, no. I didn't know Lewis until Chicago, until I met him in Chicago. He used to live right in the next block from me on South Park near 35th Street. And whenever he'd come in, he'd say, Louis is always glad to meet New Orleans musicians or anybody from New Orleans, any kind of people. So I used to go visit him, and by me playing with Little Joe Lindsey, his right-hand man, him and Little Joe Lindsey was raised up together. And Lurie used to treat me swell, and so I got to know him, and he autographed many pictures that I have in my collection. I have some great pictures of him that he gave me.
